how: One source mutation applied to the working tree, the named suite run against it, then the file restored before the next row (X14/X15's convention: `before` is the shipped source the row was run against and `after` the text that replaced it, so `before` is findable verbatim in `file`). Device rows ran on lease G15-69l63, pair-a, on 2026-11-03; the `harness:android:Checkbox` / `harness:ios:Checkbox` runs are filtered, so they satisfy nothing but their own name. Rows marked `organic` are not mutations at all: they are the test going red against the real bug before the fix landed, which is the stronger evidence and is recorded here because the logs are the proof (`gate.mjs logs --branch task/G15-checkbox`).

mutations.note: The probe that read the tree in that same run said why: a press at the row's middle — over the label — changed nothing, a press on the glyph toggled, and a press at 0.20 of the row (still on the label) delivered nothing again. mutations.note: The suggestion was good and the measurement refused it: a `Toggle` claims the whole row for hit testing and acts on the glyph only, so a layer behind the row is never asked and the label's touches die there.
